summary.oneLiner: A clean, refuses to chase corporate/system growth that would "defeat" the multi-year RAM re-mix

one-line thesis: A clean, front-loaded start to FY27: +6% QoQ on both advances and deposits, NII +32% YoY (best in 5 years), NIM defended at 4.26% (well above the conservative 3.7-3.8% full-year guide) and ROA 2.11% — with pristine asset quality (GNPA 0.74%, NNPA 0.19%, credit cost 0.33%). The whole call is a study in disciplined trade-offs: MD Ramesh Babu will walk yields down ~10 bps to retain customers, keep gold loans capped ~30-35%, refuses to chase corporate/system growth that would "defeat" the multi-year RAM re-mix, and has pre-provided INR 163 cr for war-hit sectors (textiles). Sequential optics (opex +AS-15, lower write-off recovery) mask a structurally strong quarter.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q1 FY27 | YoY / QoQ | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total business | INR 2,27,267 cr | +16% YoY / +6% QoQ | front-loaded |
| Advances | INR 1,04,680 cr | +6% QoQ | RAM 86% / Corporate 14%; retail +23% YoY |
| Deposits | INR 1,22,587 cr | +6% QoQ | CASA +9% QoQ (CA +19%, SA +4%) |
| NII | — | **+32% YoY** / +5% QoQ | highest growth in 5 years |
| NIM | **4.26%** (4.34% incl. 8 bps one-off) | +1 bp QoQ | vs FY27 guide 3.7-3.8%; despite 125 bps repo cuts since Feb-25 |
| Non-interest income | INR 442 cr | −28% QoQ (from INR 616 cr) | write-off recovery INR 103 cr (vs 216); no SR one-off (55 cr last qtr) |
| Operating profit | INR 1,096 cr | +36% YoY / −12% QoQ | seq. drop = one-offs + AS-15 opex |
| Opex | INR 769 cr | +41 cr QoQ | establishment +58 cr (AS-15 +47 cr as discount rate −40 bps) |
| Net profit | INR 756 cr | **+45% YoY** / +4% QoQ | |
| ROA | 2.11% | +1 bp QoQ | |
| GNPA / NNPA | 0.74% / 0.19% | GNPA −1% QoQ | slippages INR 138 cr (0.53% annualised), SMA-30 up 0.17%→0.22% |
| Credit cost | 0.33% annualised | — | provision INR 90 cr (NPA 68 + standard 22) |
| CRAR / LCR | 18.61% / 123.61% | — | LCR to be run 115-120% |
> One-offs distorting QoQ: last quarter had profit-on-sale INR 18 cr, SR recoveries INR 55 cr, and INR 216 cr write-off recovery (vs 103 cr now); this quarter carries AS-15 retiral hit +47 cr. INR 163 cr war-sector (textile/ceramics) provision from Q4 retained. Yield on advances 10.01% (+8 bps); cost of deposits +4 bps QoQ; investment yield 6.83%.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Credit growth:** 100-200 bps above system/industry for FY27 (calibrated — will stay ~1% above if system growth is RAM-led, more cautious if corporate-led, to avoid re-inflating corporate share); commercial/SME ~18% for the year.
- **NIM:** full-year FY27 **3.7-3.8%** guidance retained (reviewed end-Sept); Q2 expected **4%+** ("downside minimum, upside there").
- **Asset quality:** GNPA <1.5%, Net NPA <1%, slippages <1% of loan book; credit cost guided ~1% but MD "feel it can be much lower."
- **Rates:** cost of deposits +5-10 bps next quarter; yield on advances −10 bps next quarter (retention pressure); investment-book yield target ~7% by exit-quarter FY27 (from 6.83%).
- **Gold loans:** keep within ~30-35% of advances (currently ~30%).
- **FCNR-B:** double-to-triple the ~USD 130 mn base (small-ticket <USD 1 mn / <USD 50k; 7% pricing; no leverage facility).
- **Network:** 50 branches in FY27 (25 by end-Q2); cost-to-income to stay in 45-50% band (41.74% now).
- **Recoveries:** write-off recovery aim INR 500-600 cr annual (lumpy quarter-to-quarter).
- **New products:** Loan-against-Mutual-Funds launch by end-Q2; credit card extended to new-to-bank customers in H2FY27.
> Caution flagged by MD: Q1 front-loaded growth is NOT to be annualised at the same tempo.
order book & pipeline (loan pipeline / g:
- Commercial/business-banking disbursements +45% QoQ (food processing, retail/wholesale trade, engineering, transport, CRE); Small Business Group relationship model extended to 77 branches.
- Corporate/institutional +6% QoQ — highest disbursement/growth in 5 quarters (CRE, capital-market participants, EPC/infra) = "revival"; credit-substitutes +INR 171 cr.
- Retail: jewel +12%, mortgage +9%, LAP picking up (avg ticket INR 2-3 cr, commercial-heavy); housing deliberately "lying low" vs PSU pricing (7.5%); ECLGS 5.0 pipeline (2,232 commercial applicants, INR 140 cr disbursed in Q2-to-date; corporate INR 80 cr).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Gold/jewel:** ~30% of advances (cap 30-35%); agri jewel 92% of agri; LTV agri 63.7% / non-agri 56.83%; margin-call mechanism strengthened; asset quality stable despite gold-price swings.
- **Deposits:** liabilities 54% of business; retail households 72% of deposits; special TD rate +40 bps; FCNR base ~USD 130 mn; serious CA/SA focus (priority CA>SA>TD) to shave 5-10 bps cost of deposits.
- **Loan-mix rates:** fixed-rate book 29%→34%, MCLR-linked 14%→9%, EBLR 55% (mix support to yields may fade).
- **BNPL:** +2% QoQ; deliberately "lay low" pending Axio's 100%-Amazon takeover integration; cohort loss <3.5% (FLDG 5%); expects to resume by festive season.
growth verticals / optionality:
- Non-fund/guarantee income and TPP as levers to replace shrinking write-off-recovery contribution (~15-20% of profitability historically).
- NSLR investment build-up + FDL reinvestment to lift book yield to ~7% by FY27 exit.
- New products: LAMF (end-Q2), relaunched credit card (NTB in H2), GST-surrogate & open-term-loan products gaining traction.
margins & cost dynamics:
- NIM 4.26% held despite 125 bps repo cuts (Feb-25) via asset-mix recalibration + yield optimisation; fixed-rate skew deliberately raised to insulate against rate falls once FCNR/OFCB liquidity compresses rates.
- Cost of deposits creeping (+4 bps, guide +5-10 bps) on TD front-loading + FCNR/special rates; CASA push is the offset. Retention-driven yield give-up (~10 bps) is the near-term margin risk.
capex / expansion (watch slippage): - 50-branch FY27 plan (only 2 opened in Q1; 25 targeted by end-Q2) — explicit **slippage risk** flagged: premises availability/logistics/agreements delaying openings. IT/InfoSec spend non-deferrable. Staff 7,000 → 9,500.
capital allocation: - CRAR 18.61% — comfortable growth headroom; total provisions/advances 1.7% (ECL buffer); INR 163 cr war-provision retained; INR 100 cr ECL buffer built (INR 25 cr/qtr over 2 yrs). ROA-protective posture (~2%+). MD succession: MD flagged 2-yr step-down intent last quarter; Board "seized," transition/grooming to be planned.
risks & watch-items:
- **War/geopolitical exposure:** ~5% of book textiles (exports), plus ceramics/logistics — order flow down but WC utilisation steady 77-80%, no SMA spike; INR 163 cr pre-provision as cushion.
- **El Niño / monsoon:** delayed onset; agri (jewel-backed 92%) impact seen as minimal & industry-wide (still +1% vs system); some KCC postponement risk.
- **Yield compression** from retention competition (−10 bps Q2); cost of deposits rising; NIM mean-reversion toward 3.7-3.8% guide.
- **Write-off-recovery decay** (pool shrinking ~20%/yr) — needs non-fund/CASA/TPP levers to replace ~15-20% profit contribution.
- **Branch roll-out slippage;** MD succession overhang.
management quality / tone: Highly granular, candid and numbers-forward MD (Ramesh Babu) — explicitly manages expectations (Q1 not to be annualised), quantifies trade-offs (leave accounts vs concede yield), and is transparent on succession and on where sequential optics mislead. Conservative guidance (3.7-3.8% NIM vs 4.26% delivered) suggests deliberate under-promising. Strong risk framing (technical-valuation cell for LAP, margin-call mechanism for gold).
non-obvious takeaways:
- NIM 4.26% vs a 3.7-3.8% guide = large sandbag; the real question is how much of the 4%+ is sustainable as fixed-rate skew and write-off recoveries normalise.
- Corporate share deliberately taken from 45% to 14% over years — MD would rather grow only ~1% above system than re-inflate corporate to chase a corporate-led system print. Structural RAM-quality choice.
- Gold-loan sector risk is being self-capped (30-35%) even with 2% headroom — disciplined, not maxing the highest-yield product.
- El-Niño/gold logic: rising gold prices mean borrowers redeemed ornaments over 2 yrs and hold collateral to re-pledge — a demand cushion, not just a risk.
- FCNR is a customer-acquisition play (NRI relationships) more than a funding play given no leverage facility.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers (lis:
| Challenge (their words) | Beneficiary stock(s) — NSE · BSE · Sector | Loser | Why / conviction |
|---|---|---|---|
| Textile/ceramic exporters hit by West-Asia war + weak US order flow (labour shortage as Bengal/Bihar migrants return home) | _unresolved within own files_ (KVB-financed SME textile clusters, unlisted) | Export-oriented textile/ceramic SMEs; KVB ~5% book exposure | Bank pre-provided INR 163 cr; no clear listed beneficiary in our concall universe → not forcing a mapping. **Watch EU/UK FTA as offset.** |
| Housing-loan pricing war — PSU banks offering ~7.5%, no-foreclosure churn | Public-sector-bank mortgage lenders (e.g. **PNB · 532461** — Public Bank) ⭐ | KVB (cedes housing volume) | KVB explicitly "lying low" on housing vs PSU finest pricing; sector-knowledge map, not named. **Med** |
